name: decode_cmap_tile_entries
description: Scans forward in 16-bit steps for the ASCII marker CMAP, then unpacks thirty-two three-byte records, each into one 16-bit value built from the upper nibble of the third byte, the second byte and the first byte shifted left by four. The values are stored at an 8-byte stride in a global table.

name: run_nested_wait_loop
description: Calls the same helper in a nested loop of thirteen outer and twenty inner passes, then returns the helper's last result plus sixteen.

name: init_record_fields_from_args
description: Computes a record address from the index in D2 and the base pointer using a 160-byte stride, writes the low words of the two register arguments plus a fixed set of default size and position values into it, stores the pointer argument in a global, calls the helper and returns the two register arguments.

name: or_combine_five_planes
description: Walks the full table of long-words and, at each position, ORs together five values spaced at a fixed plane stride, storing each combined result sequentially in a destination array.

name: or_fold_word_columns
description: Repeats 520 blocks of a sixteen-column loop that ORs five 16-bit values read at a 32-byte stride, writing one combined word per column into a destination buffer; the source advances 160 bytes per block.

name: poll_byte_until_helper_zero
description: Sets a status byte to 36, then repeatedly calls the helper and adds eight to a byte at an offset from the caller's pointer until the helper returns zero. It returns the original first argument.

name: countdown_byte_until_helper_zero
description: Sets a status byte to 244, then repeatedly calls the helper and subtracts eight from a byte at an offset from the caller's pointer until the helper returns zero. It returns the original first argument.

name: decrement_packed_nibble_counters
description: Runs sixteen rounds of twenty-six helper calls, then for each of thirty-two words in a global table decrements each non-zero nibble among its three lowest nibbles and writes the word back.

name: accumulate_nonzero_grid_cells
description: Scans a grid of 13 rows by 20 columns of data bytes, calling a helper for each non-zero byte, and advances two running accumulators by sixteen per cell and per row. It returns both accumulators packed into one value.

name: call_helper_thirteen_times
description: Calls the same helper thirteen times in a row using a countdown counter, then returns with no value.

name: clear_thirteen_slot_words
description: Zeroes one word at the start of each of thirteen sixteen-byte slots in a global table, calls the helper, and returns the two register arguments.

name: lookup_scaled_table_word
description: Forms a 32-bit value from the high word of the first argument and a word at a fixed offset from a pointer, reduces it modulo ten and halves it, then indexes a 22-byte-stride table with the result. It stores the word read into a global, calls the helper and returns the first argument.

name: write_chip_register_from_table
description: Looks up a 16-bit offset in a 22-byte-stride table using the second argument, writes the first argument as a word into the custom chip register at that offset, and returns both arguments.

name: clear_four_words_set_flag
description: Zeroes four consecutive words of a global array, stores fifteen into a global value, then calls the helper and returns the two register arguments.

name: copy_sprite_def_free_slot
description: Looks up a 22-byte definition by the first argument and checks a global bitmask and a pointer field. It finds the first of four slots whose word is zero, optionally calls a helper and sets a flag bit, then writes the definition's pointer and position words to custom chip registers and sets the slot's bit in a global mask with bit fifteen set.

name: clear_flag_bit_in_records
description: Calls the helper once, then clears bit one of the byte at offset twenty in each of thirty-three 22-byte records in a global table.

name: update_global_word_by_division
description: Divides a 32-bit value built from the high word of the D2 register and a global word by a constant, XORs the quotient into that global word, then rotates the word left by nine bits and XORs in a constant. It returns the two register arguments unchanged.

name: xor_then_rotate_table_bytes
description: Walks a 900-byte table from the last entry back to the first, XORing each byte with four and rotating it left by three bits within the byte.

name: rotate_then_xor_table_bytes
description: Walks a 900-byte table from the last entry back to the first, rotating each byte left by five bits and then XORing it with four.

name: set_pointer_and_call_helpers
description: Calls the helper, stores a pointer into a global at the global base plus the D7 word times five, then calls the helper twice more.

name: compare_nul_terminated_strings
description: Walks two byte pointers forward together, comparing bytes until the first string reaches its terminating zero or the bytes differ, then returns.

name: handle_key_input_state
description: Dispatches a key code by state. In the active state a space runs a helper three times, a code of two clears five state globals, and the letters B, D, M, W, T, C, H, G, F, S, K, E, L and R are mapped to numeric values stored in a global before a helper call; in the idle state a code of two clears another flag.

name: poll_serial_byte_change
description: Sets bit six of a global control byte, compares the current byte with the previously stored value, and when they differ and bit zero is set calls the helper. It then clears bit six and returns.

name: setup_pointer_between_helper_calls
description: Calls the helper four times, stores the address of a global as a pointer, copies that pointer into a RAM word, then sets the pointer to a fixed constant and calls the helper four more times.

name: set_flags_and_update_records
description: Sets the low two bits of a global flag byte, then walks thirty-three 22-byte records and, for each record whose second long is non-zero, overwrites its first long with a value from a global.

name: load_sfx_table_entries
description: Calls a library routine through a pointer and, if it returns non-zero, walks thirty-three table entries. Each entry whose second field is zero is loaded through a second library call, stopping early when a load returns zero, and a final library call follows. The referenced text is a sound effect file name.

name: call_pending_entry_callbacks
description: Walks thirty-three 22-byte records and, for each whose first long is non-zero and second long is zero, calls a routine from the library table through a pointer derived from the library base.

name: open_dos_library_handle
description: Calls an exec library routine through a pointer built from the library base and stores its return value in a global handle. The referenced text is the dos library name.

name: wait_for_nonzero_timer_word
description: Busy-waits until the word formed from a global byte repeated twice is non-zero, copies that word into another global, then writes a constant with bit fifteen set to the global control word and returns.

name: fill_eight_split_words
description: Writes eight 8-byte slots in a global table, each receiving the high and low words of a running 32-bit value taken from a global, which advances by a fixed step after each slot.

name: fill_five_split_words
description: Writes five 8-byte slots in a global table, storing the high and low words of the input register in each slot, and advancing the register by a fixed large step per slot.

name: call_helper_seven_times
description: Calls the same helper seven times in sequence and returns. The referenced text names two tile image files, but the routine itself only makes the calls.

name: transpose_byte_columns
description: Calls a helper twice, then copies 640 bytes from a source buffer into a destination in sequence, reading them with a stride of forty bytes across two passes of forty rows by eight columns. The referenced text is a character graphics file name.

name: run_helper_sequence_with_settings
description: Runs a fixed sequence of helper calls, setting one global to six and later to five and a second global to two 16-bit constants at points in the sequence. It repeats one helper until it returns zero and makes two final calls. The referenced text names two intro graphics files.

name: edit_five_char_text_entry
description: Fills a five-character buffer with underscore placeholders, then loops reading key codes: code two clears the buffer back to placeholders, code one deletes the last character, other codes are appended up to five characters, and codes three or four end the loop. It then calls helpers and clears a global when the final code is zero.

name: close_library_and_reset_state
description: Calls a helper, then calls a library close routine through a pointer built from the library base, resets a global to fifteen, restores it from a saved pointer, sets it to a fixed 16-bit value, and calls a helper that starts the copper list.

name: load_entries_until_zero
description: Walks a table of three-word entries, calling a library function through a pointer for each to store its result in the entry, and stops when the call returns zero. It returns the entry's second field when that field is negative, otherwise zero.

name: walk_entries_until_negative
description: Walks a table of three-word entries, skipping zero entries, returning when it reaches a negative entry, and calling a library function through a pointer for each positive one.

name: stub_interrupt_handler_undecoded
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this four-instruction routine, so its behaviour is not recovered. The listed facts show one call to another routine, a touch of the interrupt request register, and that it is referenced as a handler from data.

name: handle_flag_bit_five_event
description: Tests bit five of a global byte and, when it is set, resets the byte to thirty-two and calls the helper. Otherwise it returns immediately.

name: initialise_display_and_copy_tables
description: Saves two control words, disables interrupts and DMA by writing a value with bit fifteen clear, zeroes a large block of memory, copies two 600-long tables into destination buffers, copies a table of words into a list, calls two helpers, writes two custom registers and waits for a busy flag before restoring the saved words.

name: call_helpers_store_record_field
description: Calls one helper when bit two of a global flag is set, then calls five helpers in sequence and stores the constant 112 into a record field at offset 156.

name: advance_scan_and_divide
description: Decrements a countdown word and, when it reaches zero, resets it to eight and advances a scan index past entries equal to minus one. It writes a fixed sequence of constants to a global and returns the quotient and remainder of its second argument divided by its first, packed into one 32-bit value.

name: advance_scan_and_setup_blitter
description: Decrements a countdown word and, when it reaches zero, resets it to eight and advances a scan index past entries equal to minus one. It then writes a fixed sequence of six constants to blitter registers and returns its arguments unchanged.

name: draw_blit_grid_rotating_mask
description: Waits for the busy flag to clear, advances a column offset in a table, then fills a grid of twenty-two rows by eight columns, writing blitter register values while a mask rotates left by two bits each cell. It restores the blitter registers it changed before returning.

name: build_bounce_entry_list
description: Updates a step value and bounces it between two limits, using the sum of two globals as the test value. It then builds thirty-two four-word list entries in memory from a global table and the running value, each ending with a fixed end marker.

name: copy_words_until_zero_terminator
description: Copies 16-bit words from one global buffer to another, stopping after the last word that precedes a zero word, then stores one global into another global.

name: build_indexed_entry_table
description: Builds 105 eight-byte entries, each holding a fixed byte, a byte from a global, a zero word and a long read from a small table indexed by the next source byte. A source byte of 255 is replaced by a global value.

name: fill_cycling_offset_entries
description: Fills 105 eight-byte entries with a running code byte, a byte made from a source byte plus a cycling value from zero to three, a count byte and a zero. A source byte of 255 is replaced by a global value.

name: dispatch_audio_channel_mode
description: Dispatches on the low two bits of its first argument. Mode zero scrambles a 16-word table with rotate, add and XOR steps and calls four channel helpers, mode one builds channel tables and pointers from embedded data, mode two stores a masked value, and mode three fills one of four channel records from a lookup table.

name: reset_record_fields_from_source
description: Clears several word and byte fields of a record, copies a long from the data pointer into one field, stores a fixed address constant in another, sets a byte to 63 and sets a flag byte to one.

name: scramble_table_and_run_counters
description: Fills a 16-word table from a rotate, add and XOR sequence, decrements a countdown byte that wraps when it goes negative, and calls four helpers. It then decrements four 16-bit counters, calling a helper for each non-zero one and setting a flag for each zero one.

name: advance_sequence_channel_state
description: Advances one sequence channel record: it reads table values and a byte stream, updates an accumulator and step counters, and calls a handler from a jump table when a command byte is present. The pseudo-code is truncated in the bundle, so the remaining behaviour is not recovered.

name: store_nibble_field_return_mask
description: Stores the low four bits of the second byte argument into a record field at offset forty-seven and returns the first argument ORed with 126.

name: store_low_nibble_field
description: Stores the low four bits of the second byte argument into a record field at offset forty-seven and returns nothing.

name: install_vectors_and_init_hardware
description: Stores its argument in a global, writes jump-instruction opcodes into low memory vectors and issues a software trap. It clears eight custom registers and points eight pointer registers at a global, clears a block of globals, runs a sequence of helper calls with fixed addresses, then calls through a pointer held in a global.

name: install_jump_vectors_bad_tail
description: Writes jump and return opcodes with handler addresses into fixed memory locations and calls several helpers. The decompiler then reaches an undecodable instruction and truncates the routine, so its tail is not recovered.

name: handle_serial_status_flag
description: When bit three of a global status byte is set, sets the byte to 255 and marks bit six busy. If a transformed copy of the previous value is below 249 it calls a helper and stores the result, then clears the busy bit and resets the status byte to eight.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing any work. The listed facts show only that another routine takes its address.

name: handle_serial_status_store_result
description: Follows the same serial status pattern as its neighbour: a set status bit sets the byte to 255 and marks it busy, and a helper result is stored in a separate word when the transformed previous value is below 249. The status byte is then reset to eight.

name: handle_serial_status_alt_store
description: Same serial status pattern as its neighbour: when a status bit is set it sets the byte to 255 and marks it busy, calls a helper when the transformed previous value is below 249 and stores the result in a second location, then clears the busy bit and resets the status byte to eight.

name: write_fixed_patch_words_jump
description: Writes two fixed 32-bit words, a jump instruction whose target is a helper, and a short branch word into fixed memory locations.

name: patch_jump_vectors_bad_tail
description: Writes jump and return opcodes and handler addresses into memory vectors, then calls a blitter-wait routine and several helpers. The decompiler then reaches an undecodable instruction and truncates the routine, so its tail is not recovered.

name: patch_jump_vectors_short_tail
description: Writes jump and return opcodes into memory, then calls a blitter-wait routine and several helpers. An undecodable instruction truncates the decompiled routine, so its tail is not recovered.

name: stub_infinite_idle_loop
description: Contains only an infinite loop and does no visible work, so it never returns. The decompiler removed the unreachable blocks around it.

name: stub_infinite_loop_hold
description: Contains only an infinite loop with no visible work, so it never returns. The listed facts show one call to another routine, but the decompiled body never reaches it.

name: set_global_control_word
description: Writes a fixed control word with bit fifteen set into a global and returns. The listed facts also name the interrupt request register and three further calls, which the decompiled body does not show.

name: call_routine_then_pointer_slot
description: Calls a routine, then calls a function pointer read at a fixed offset from the A2 register, and returns the second argument unchanged.

name: call_helper_then_slot_pointer
description: Calls a helper, then calls a function pointer read at a fixed offset from the A2 register, and returns the second argument unchanged.

name: return_fixed_size_constant
description: Returns the constant 512 with no other work. The referenced text names a save file, which this routine does not use.

name: return_fixed_size_alternate
description: Returns the same constant 512 as its neighbour with no other work. The referenced text names an indoor save file, which the code does not use.

name: patch_matching_table_entries
description: Scans a fixed region of about sixteen thousand words, and wherever a word matches the second argument and is followed by the value eighty-eight, writes the first argument as a long at that place.

name: set_blit_word_and_wait
description: Writes a fixed word into a record field at offset eighty-eight, then busy-waits until the blitter busy flag clears.

name: store_word_then_wait_blitter
description: Stores the D4 register word into a record field at offset eighty-eight, then busy-waits until the blitter busy flag clears.

name: store_d6_word_then_wait
description: Stores the D6 register word into a record field at offset eighty-eight through the A5 base, then busy-waits until the blitter busy flag clears.

name: return_fixed_long_constant
description: Returns a fixed 32-bit constant and does no other work.

name: dispatch_special_word_codes
description: Compares its low-word argument with two adjacent special codes. Each code calls a helper and then a pointer at offset eight from A2, while any other value is passed through a pointer at offset forty from a global base and returned unchanged.

name: issue_bootblock_read_requests
description: Sets up an I/O request with a fixed destination address, a length of three kilobytes, an offset of one kilobyte and a read command, then calls the library I/O routine repeatedly while a flag in the request is non-zero.

name: reset_sprite_registers_then_run
description: Clears eight sprite control registers and points eight sprite pointer registers at a global, then clears a block of globals. It calls helpers at a set of fixed addresses and finally calls through a pointer held in a global.

name: delay_by_countdown_loop
description: Burns time by decrementing a 16-bit counter from its maximum value until it wraps back to zero, then returns.

name: write_descending_word_values
description: Writes every 16-bit value from the maximum down to one into a global word, stopping before zero. The listed facts say this touches the background colour register.

name: poll_helper_until_zero
description: Repeatedly calls a helper and loops until it returns zero, then returns.

name: transfer_eleven_block_groups
description: Divides a request into groups of eleven units and loops over them, copying or skipping up to eleven units of 512 bytes per pass. It advances the destination pointer by 512 bytes per unit and calls helpers around each pass, stopping at a fixed upper limit.

name: fill_alternating_pattern_longs
description: If the first longword of a buffer does not already hold an alternating-bit pattern, writes that pattern into a run of 417 longwords.

name: scan_slots_mark_full_entries
description: Runs eleven passes of helper calls, and on passes where a flag is set reads a byte from a helper and returns early if it is below eleven. Otherwise it writes an all-ones word into a global table at an index derived from its argument.

name: wait_for_sync_value
description: Runs a helper three times per pass for a counted number of passes, then polls a helper up to eleven times until it returns twenty-eight, returning early if that value is never seen.

name: program_blitter_decode_passes
description: Programs blitter control, mask and pointer registers from a sector offset computed by a helper, using alternating-bit mask constants. It then reprograms the pointers and size for a second pass and calls helpers around each step.

name: step_position_modulo_eleven
description: Computes a starting position modulo eleven from its arguments, then calls a helper once for each step of a counted loop, advancing the position and wrapping it back to zero after ten.

name: start_blitter_copy_pass
description: Computes three blitter pointer values from its input and two address registers, programs the blitter control and size registers for a two-row copy, and then calls a helper.

name: verify_sector_header_and_sync
description: Checks each entry of a block for an alternating-bit marker and a fixed sync word, and checks paired values for a match. It returns numbered error codes from twenty-one to twenty-six for the failing check, or a byte taken from the D3 register when all checks pass.

name: adjust_top_bit_by_flag
description: Reads the byte at the pointer and tests the low bit of the byte before it. If that bit is clear it sets the top bit unless bit six is already set; if it is set it clears the top bit, then writes the byte back.

name: verify_checksum_of_longs
description: Computes an alternating-bit XOR checksum over ten longwords taken from the buffer, or from helper results when the flag is set. It compares this with a helper result and a status byte, returning zero on a match and error code twenty-seven otherwise.

name: merge_alternating_bit_longs
description: Takes the alternating-bit positions of two consecutive longwords and merges them into one value, with the bits of the first longword shifted up by one.

name: xor_fold_masked_longs
description: XOR-folds a run of longwords whose count is a quarter of the second argument, then masks the result with the alternating-bit pattern and returns it.

name: shift_long_and_word_pair
description: Shifts a longword left by a count derived from the D2 register and the following word right by the same count, combining the two into one 32-bit result.

name: call_three_helpers_in_sequence
description: Calls three helpers in order and returns with no result. Two other routines call it.

name: store_masked_alternating_bits
description: Computes a mask from the alternating-bit positions of its argument, shifts it to combine with neighbouring bits, and clears its sign bit when the flag byte before the target is set. It then stores the result, combined with the argument's alternating-bit positions, through the pointer.

name: search_block_for_sync_index
description: Scans a block of words for an alternating-bit marker, then compares the values that follow against a table of patterns. It returns the matching table index counting down by two, or minus one when the block ends without a match.

name: copy_word_or_start_blitter
description: When its count argument is non-zero it copies the word before a pointer through a helper into a destination. Otherwise it calls a helper and programs blitter control, shift, size and pointer registers before calling a routine.

name: start_blitter_decode_pass
description: Computes a shifted parameter with a helper, programs blitter control, shift, size and pointer registers for a decode pass, and then calls a routine.

name: wait_status_bit_six_clear
description: Busy-waits while bit six of the status byte at offset two from the A2 register is set, then returns.

name: reset_track_record_fields
description: Sets a long field at offset sixty-eight to all ones and a word at offset one hundred twelve to an alternating-bit value. It also clears three word fields at offsets one hundred, ninety-eight and one hundred two.

name: start_disk_dma_read
description: When the zero flag is set, calls a routine, then points the disk pointer register at a buffer, writes disk-control and DMA-control words, and starts a read of a fixed length. Otherwise it returns without starting a transfer.

name: start_disk_dma_write
description: When bit three of a status byte is set, points the disk pointer at a buffer, writes control and DMA words, starts a write of a fixed length and returns the routine's result. Otherwise it returns twenty-eight.

name: wait_disk_transfer_done
description: Polls a disk status word for a large fixed number of passes. When bit one is set it writes the disk length register to disable the transfer, sets a control field to two and returns zero; if the count runs out it disables the transfer and returns minus one.

name: deselect_drive_bit
description: Clears one drive-select bit in the CIA-B port register, choosing the bit from a stored drive index.

name: wait_drive_ready_status
description: Writes all ones to a control register, calls two routines, then polls a status bit for a fixed count until it clears. It returns zero on success or error code thirty-four on timeout.

name: seek_drive_to_track
description: Compares the stored track position with the target track, steps the head once per track of difference, records the new position and returns zero. If the stored position is negative and non-zero it returns a value from a helper instead.

name: wait_drive_index_clear
description: Polls a status bit up to eighty-six times, calling a helper on each pass. When the bit clears it zeroes a word in a table for the selected drive and returns zero; otherwise it returns error code thirty.

name: update_port_control_bits
description: Reads a port value from a helper, clears bit one when the second argument is non-negative, sets bit zero and stores the result in a global, then calls a helper.

name: delay_after_port_write
description: Writes the value from a helper into a global, then counts down a fixed delay loop of about fifteen thousand steps before returning.

name: spin_down_argument_counter
description: Decrements its first argument register until it reaches zero, then returns.

name: build_drive_select_port_value
description: Builds a CIA-B port value by clearing one bit chosen from a stored drive index, and clearing a second bit when that drive's flag word is odd. It returns the value together with the second argument.

name: init_sprites_trap_then_run
description: Issues a software trap, clears eight sprite control registers and points eight sprite pointer registers at a global. It clears a block of globals, calls helpers at fixed addresses and finally calls through a pointer held in a global.

name: clear_sprites_and_call_pointer
description: Clears eight sprite control registers and points eight sprite pointer registers at a global. It clears a block of globals, calls helpers at fixed addresses and finally calls through a pointer held in a global.

name: spin_word_countdown_wrap
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter from its maximum value until it wraps back to zero, then returns.

name: write_descending_word_values
description: Writes every 16-bit value from the maximum down to one into a global word, stopping before zero. The listed facts say this touches the background colour register.

description: When the zero flag is set, calls a routine, then points the disk pointer register at a buffer, writes disk-control and DMA-control words, and starts a read of a fixed length. Otherwise it returns without starting a transfer.

name: start_disk_dma_write
description: When bit three of a status byte is set, points the disk pointer at a buffer, writes control and DMA words, starts a write of a fixed length and returns the routine's result. Otherwise it returns twenty-eight.

name: wait_disk_transfer_done
description: Polls a disk status word for a large fixed number of passes. When bit one is set it writes the disk length register to disable the transfer, sets a control field to two and returns zero; if the count runs out it disables the transfer and returns minus one.

name: write_inverted_drive_bit
description: Writes the bitwise inverse of a single bit, chosen from a stored drive index, into a global and returns.

name: deselect_drive_bit
description: Clears one drive-select bit in the CIA-B port register, choosing the bit from a stored drive index.

name: wait_drive_ready_status
description: Writes all ones to a control register, calls two routines, then polls a status bit for a fixed count until it clears. It returns zero on success or error code thirty-four on timeout.

name: seek_drive_to_track
description: Compares the stored track position with the target track, steps the head once per track of difference, records the new position and returns zero. If the stored position is negative and non-zero it returns a value from a helper instead.

name: wait_drive_index_clear
description: Polls a status bit up to eighty-six times, calling a helper on each pass. When the bit clears it zeroes a word in a table for the selected drive and returns zero; otherwise it returns error code thirty.

name: update_port_control_bits
description: Reads a port value from a helper, clears bit one when the second argument is non-negative, sets bit zero and stores the result in a global, then calls a helper.

name: delay_after_port_write
description: Writes the value from a helper into a global, then counts down a fixed delay loop of about fifteen thousand steps before returning.

name: spin_down_argument_counter
description: Decrements its first argument register until it reaches zero, then returns.

name: build_drive_select_port_value
description: Builds a CIA-B port value by clearing one bit chosen from a stored drive index, and clearing a second bit when that drive's flag word is odd. It returns the value together with the second argument.

name: run_six_block_passes
description: Repeats six times: calls a helper with the current argument and a function address, runs a helper sixteen times, then advances the argument with another helper call. It returns nothing.

name: run_six_block_passes
description: Repeats six times: calls a helper with the current argument and a function address, runs a helper sixteen times, then advances the argument with another helper call. It returns nothing.

name: adjust_packed_bitfields_upward
description: Compares three packed 3-bit fields of two words against a threshold scaled to each field. Where the second word's field exceeds that threshold and differs from the first word's field, the first word's field is incremented, and the combined fields are written back to the first word.

name: copy_header_then_fill_words
description: Copies eight longwords from the pointer argument into globals, then runs seven passes that call a helper and store sixteen returned words in sequence into a buffer.

name: decrement_packed_bitfields
description: Decrements each of three packed 3-bit fields in a word, at bits zero, four and eight, leaving any field already at zero unchanged, and returns the combined word.

name: stub_unimplemented_register_save
description: Saves the register arguments into globals, then reaches an unimplemented instruction, so the decompiler truncates the routine. Only the register saves are recovered.

name: wait_status_pulse_then_clear
description: Calls a fixed-address routine and returns zero if it returns zero. Otherwise it calls a helper, counts while bit six of a status byte is set, waits until that bit is set again, then clears the byte and returns part of the helper's result.

name: wait_status_pulse_then_clear
description: Calls a fixed-address routine and returns zero if it returns zero. Otherwise it calls a helper, counts while bit six of a status byte is set, waits until that bit is set again, then clears the byte and returns part of the helper's result.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reached undecodable instruction data after a few helper calls and a store of a fixed value, so the routine is truncated and only those steps are recovered.

name: stub_no_decompiled_function
description: The decompiler produced no function body for this routine, so its behaviour is not recovered. The listed facts show sixteen calls to other routines and touches of the interrupt enable, DMA control and interrupt request registers.

name: spin_word_countdown_to_zero
description: Decrements a 32-bit counter starting from the 16-bit maximum down to zero as a delay, then returns.

name: repeat_write_fifteen_bad_tail
description: Writes the value fifteen to a global in a long countdown loop, then reaches undecodable instruction data that truncates the routine. The listed facts show it touches the background colour register.

name: set_control_word_after_calls
description: Calls a helper six times, writes a fixed control word with bit ten set into a global, clears a second global and calls a helper once more.

name: split_words_into_four_planes
description: Copies 200 rows of twenty groups of four words, splitting each group's four words across four destination planes whose pointers advance by one word per group.

name: wait_status_pulse_return_byte
description: Waits while bit six of a status byte is set, then waits until it is set, and returns the original low byte of its argument with the upper bytes from the status read.

name: return_low_word_sign_extended
description: Returns its low word argument sign-extended to 32 bits with no other work. The listed facts mark the code as an unreached gap, so no caller is confirmed.

name: double_sixteen_words_into_table
description: Calls a helper, then copies sixteen words from the pointer argument into a global table, doubling each value, and returns its two register arguments.

name: fill_block_with_ones
description: Writes all-ones longwords across 319 blocks of eight longwords starting at the pointer argument, advancing the pointer by eight longs per block.

name: clear_block_of_longs
description: Writes zero into 319 blocks of eight longwords starting at the pointer argument, advancing the pointer by eight longs per block.

name: call_helper_four_times
description: Calls the same helper four times in sequence and returns.

name: write_interrupt_disable_then_enable
description: Writes a value with bit fifteen clear, then one with bit fifteen set, to a global control word and returns.

name: store_control_word_and_pointer
description: Writes a fixed control word with bit fifteen set to a global, copies it into a second global and stores the first global's address in a pointer global, then returns.

name: configure_display_and_copper
description: Writes display window, data fetch and modulo registers, sets colour and bitplane control words, points the copper at a global list and enables the DMA controls. It then returns the value of one custom register.

name: install_interrupt_vector_pointer
description: Writes a value with bit fifteen clear, then the address of a routine, then a value with bit fifteen set to global words, and returns its byte argument unchanged.

name: install_interrupt_vector_setup
description: Writes a value with bit fifteen clear, then the address of a routine, then a value with bit fifteen set to global words, and returns with no result.

name: spin_until_tick_compare
description: Loops while a global counter compared with itself plus the first argument reports less-than, so the wait only ends when that comparison changes. It returns nothing.

name: tick_and_call_handler_table
description: Increments a global counter, calls each non-null entry of an eight-entry handler table, and sets a global control word to thirty-two.

name: read_and_clear_pending_word
description: Returns the current value of a global word and resets that word to zero.

name: return_routine_address
description: Returns the address of a routine with no other work. The listed facts mark this as an unreached gap.

name: configure_timer_and_call_helpers
description: Writes a control value with bit fifteen set, a routine address and several timer-style constants to globals, then calls two helpers. The listed facts name the timer and interrupt registers.

name: check_serial_status_store_result
description: Sets a status byte to eight and, when bit three of it is set, calls a helper. It stores a second helper's result in a global when a transformed copy of the first result is below 249.

name: write_marker_then_clear
description: Writes all ones to a global byte, then writes zero to it, and returns.

name: stub_empty_return_text_ref
description: Returns immediately with no work. The referenced text is a row of keyboard characters, which this routine does not use.

name: set_blitter_masks_and_offsets
description: Writes a fixed control word with bits fifteen, ten and six set to a global, sets the two blitter mask registers to all ones, and clears the two blitter control registers.

name: forward_to_helper_call
description: The decompiled body contains only one call to another routine, while the listed facts describe a 207-instruction routine with three calls. The remaining behaviour is not recovered.

name: call_helper_then_store_ones
description: Calls a helper, then writes an all-ones word through the pointer register argument.

name: call_helper_store_word_offset
description: Calls a helper, then stores the low word of the second argument at offset twelve from the A6 base, and returns both arguments.

name: call_helper_store_second_word
description: Calls a helper, then stores the low word of the second argument at offset fourteen from the A6 base, and returns both arguments.

name: store_argument_then_call_helper
description: Writes the low word of the first argument into a global, calls a helper, stores the A6 register value at a fixed RAM location, and returns the first argument.

name: init_record_from_stack_args
description: Reads four words from its stack arguments and calls a helper. Unless a stack value is negative, it fills a record with those words, the helper's result, zero fields and the constants fifteen, one hundred, six and two; when a global is negative it also calls helpers and sets two table words to all ones.

name: find_first_free_record
description: Scans up to sixteen records spaced forty-eight bytes apart in a fixed table, returning the index of the first whose leading word is negative, or minus one if none is.

name: return_first_word_argument
description: Returns its first word argument unchanged with no other work. Eight other routines call it.

name: reset_sixteen_record_markers
description: Sets the leading word of each of sixteen records, spaced forty-eight bytes apart in a fixed table, to all ones, then clears two global words.

name: call_helper_per_string_char
description: Stores the A6 register value in a global, then calls a helper for each character of a zero-terminated byte string at the pointer argument.

name: call_helper_per_string_char
description: Stores the A6 register value in a global, then calls a helper for each character of a zero-terminated byte string at the pointer argument.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing any work. The listed facts show only that it is referenced by address from elsewhere.

name: dispatch_carriage_return_char
description: Stores the A6 register value in a global, then, if the character argument is a carriage return, calls one helper. Otherwise it calls a helper with the A0 pointer and another helper.

name: dispatch_carriage_return_simple
description: Calls one helper when the character argument is a carriage return, and otherwise calls two helpers.

name: advance_two_axis_counters
description: Increments a first counter at offset eight until it reaches the limit minus one stored at offset four. It then increments a second counter at offset ten and resets the first, wrapping both to zero at their limits.

name: advance_second_axis_counter
description: Resets the counter at offset eight to zero, then increments the counter at offset ten unless it has reached the limit minus one stored at offset six. When it has reached that limit, both counters are reset to zero.
